predictions.text: Dr. Charles P. Steinmetz, world's famous electrical wizard recently caused a great sensation by engineering an electrical storm in his laboratory at Schnectady, N.Y., having all the thrills of a regular storm. Thunder was heard in its heavy velocity and the lightning generator throwing off 120,000 volts caused a mighty flash to strike a tree branch placed in the room for experiments, splitting the wood as a streak of lightning would do to any harmless tree, and throwing the fragments 25 feet. Our photo of the lightning generator, shows the vivid white flash as the moment of discharge of the man-made lightning bolt in Dr. Steinmetz's laboratory. This picture, incidently is the first ever made of an artificial lighting bolt in action. The engineers shown are: Dr. Charles P. Steinmetz, J.L.R. Hayden and N.A. Lougee. Photo by General Electric Company. 3/4/22.
